title.narrative: Strengthening Free Expression in Northern Sri Lanka

description.narrative: The aim of the project is "to strengthen freedom of expression, internet freedom and independent journalism in Sri Lanka's Northern Province by building youth and journalist capacity to counter hate speech and misinformation in Tamil-language online spaces, and by generating evidence-based civil-society engagement on the digital-rights legal environment". The project is built on three integrated objectives: • Objective 1 - Youth engagement and a hate-speech response mechanism: Build a cohort of 20 students (gender-balanced, drawn from across the five districts) from the Department of Media Studies, University of Jaffna. After a two-day residential training, the youth deliver community level awareness programmes in their home districts and operate a youth-led mechanism to identify, counter and report hate speech in Tamil-language online spaces, supported by a structured six-month mentoring cycle. • Objective 2 - Northern Journalist Forum and a Tamil-language fact-checking platform: Convene Tamil-language journalists from the five Northern districts into a peer forum with a constitution, code of conduct and rotating coordination committee; deliver targeted training; and launch a Tamil-language fact-checking platform (website plus active social media) that publishes regular verifications, debunks and explainers under Forum editorial oversight. • Objective 3 - Civil-society review of the Online Safety Act: Undertake a structured review of Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act with legal experts, civil-society organizations, journalists and academics; document case studies and impacts on free expression in the North; and publish a bilingual (Tamil + English) policy report with concrete recommendations, disseminated through a public roundtable, targeted briefings and media coverage.
